items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: Mr. Labot and Mr. Maloney they thought it was great the way I was massing the business, you know, because I'd watch it good.

ctx.x: Yeah. We got out of the Depression. I see. Did you do any work in the Jitneys they had around here then? No, not here. Not here.

In town. I wouldn't play the Jitneys town, I would play Jitneys down there. Down there the Jitneys town was different, you see it was too hard. In the walls it was too hard. Yeah, it was too hard. Down there we had the dancers barricades, the dance hall. And we'd play a number, well I'd say a holy number. This would a crowd to get in and make a dance. And by the time the one to leave from here and go around and get back there and get stopped. Now we'd take a rest right then until the last one get out the ring.…
Well I think they have a big dance hall at Raceland. Now they play rock and roll.
